# clean-links

> Decide whether two links point at the same **Resource** (the page a person
> would call "the same thing"), so shared links can be de-duplicated and counted.
> It follows redirects to each link's final URL, strips known tracking params
> (ClearURLs), and compares what's left. Async-first, optional persistent cache.

For coding agents **integrating** clean-links into their own code. `import
clean_links` (PyPI `clean_links`). Short and self-contained — safe to read in
full, or stop after Quick start and come back for a section by name:

- Compare or group links → **Quick start** (the common case; enough on its own)
- Persist / scale across runs → **Persistent cache**
- Output looks wrong, or "will this be correct?" → **Contracts**
- Exact signatures, `Engine`, `Options` → **API surface**
- Something misbehaves → **Gotchas**

Full vocabulary: docs/glossary.md.

## Quick start (sync — makes live network requests)

```python
from clean_links import are_equivalent_sync, group_sync

are_equivalent_sync("https://bit.ly/x", "https://trib.al/y")   # -> bool

groups = group_sync(["https://bit.ly/x", "https://trib.al/y", "https://ex.com/z"])
# -> {canonical_key: [input_urls...]}   the first two resolve to one Resource:
# {"https://www.bloomberg.com/...": ["https://bit.ly/x", "https://trib.al/y"],
#  "https://ex.com/z": ["https://ex.com/z"]}
```

Every `*_sync` is an `asyncio.run()` wrapper over an async coroutine of the same
name — drop the suffix and `await` it.

## Persistent cache across runs (the main recipe)

Resolve each link at most once and reuse it across runs/processes by giving an
`Engine` a `SqliteStore`:

```python
import asyncio
from clean_links import Engine, SqliteStore

async def main(urls):
    store = SqliteStore("cache.sqlite")   # created if missing (WAL)
    engine = Engine(store=store)
    try:
        return await engine.group(urls)
    finally:
        await engine.aclose()   # closes the Engine's OWN http client...
        await store.close()     # ...NOT a store you passed in — that's yours

asyncio.run(main(urls))
```

**Ownership rule:** `Engine.aclose()` frees only what the Engine created. A
`store`/`fetcher`/`limiter` you pass in, you close yourself. (Module-level
helpers build and close their own Engine per call, so a `store=` handed to them
is also left open — use an explicit `Engine` for a persistent cache.)

## Contracts that keep your usage correct

- **Endpoint is truth.** The key is computed from a link's final URL; the stored
  redirect graph is only a cache.
- **Caching:** a reachable resolution is reused for `success_ttl` (30 d); a
  failure is negatively cached for `failure_ttl` (6 h) then retried — so a
  transiently-down or blocked host recovers on a later run by itself.
- **Failures never raise inside `group`/`canonical_key`.** An unreachable link
  gets a best-effort key from the deepest URL seen (bias to **false-split**): it
  forms its own bucket instead of wrongly merging. Corollary — a duplicate
  reachable *only* via a redirect that can't be followed won't be detected.
- **Gateways** (`google.com/url?q=…`, `l.facebook.com/l.php?u=…`) are unwrapped
  from the URL with **no request**; **shorteners** (bit.ly, t.co) are followed.
- **Fetch:** `HEAD`, retried as `GET` on 403/405/501; `Retry-After` honored on
  429/503.
- **Polite by default:** ≤2 in-flight and ≥1 s apart **per registrable domain**
  (`www.nature.com` == `nature.com`), unbounded across hosts — many-host batches
  are fast; one busy host crawls ~1/s.
- **Query kept by default** (only known trackers stripped, to avoid false
  merges). `group(urls, show_query_sensitivity=True)` returns
  `{"groups": …, "query_sensitive": [[urls that would merge if the query were
  dropped], …]}` so you can audit which params actually matter.

## API surface

Network-following (async + a `*_sync` twin; all accept `**engine_kwargs` →
`Engine(...)`):
- `are_equivalent(a, b) -> bool`
- `group(urls, show_query_sensitivity=False) -> dict`
- `canonical_key(url) -> str` — resolve, then key
- `resolve(url) -> Resolution(url, endpoint, chain, reachable, error, hops)`

Pure (sync, **no network** — canonicalize the URL as given):
- `clean_url(url, keep_query=True, keep_fragment=True) -> str` — strip known trackers
- `key_of(url, options=None, strip_query=False) -> str` — full canonical key as-is

⚠️ **`key_of` (no network) vs `canonical_key` (follows redirects)** is the easy
mix-up. For "same after redirects," you want `canonical_key`/`are_equivalent`.

`Engine(fetcher=None, store=None, limiter=None, options=None)` — async methods
`resolve`, `canonical_key(url, strip_query=False)`, `are_equivalent`, `group`,
`aclose`. Inject a backend via the `Fetcher`/`Store`/`RateLimiter` protocols;
`FakeFetcher(routes=…, fail=…)` is the deterministic test double.

`Options` defaults: `max_redirects=30, verify_tls=True, timeout=9.0,
fold_scheme=True, fold_www=True, fold_trailing_slash=True,
success_ttl=2_592_000, failure_ttl=21_600`.

## Gotchas

- `are_equivalent_sync`/`group_sync` **hit the network** — not pure string ops.
- Passed-in `store`/`fetcher` → **you** close it, not `aclose()`.
- `SqliteStore` is **single-process**, no busy timeout — don't run two writers on
  one cache file (risk `SQLITE_BUSY`, which degrades a link to a best-effort key).
- Need no-network canonicalization? `key_of`, not `canonical_key`.
- A host serving an **incomplete TLS chain** fails verification (Python doesn't
  AIA-fetch missing intermediates) → resolves unreachable. `Options(verify_tls=
  False)` only if you accept the risk.
- Predicting whether a re-run hits the network: reachable links land in the
  `resolved` table, failures as `error` hops — an unreachable link has *no*
  `resolved` row, so walk its cached hop chain, don't just check `resolved`.
